Tom owns a very large garden and is passionate about flowers. He has hired two gardeners, Alex and Benni, who are responsible for taking care of the plants on his 30 flower beds. Both gardeners are free to choose their own working hours and to decide how to divide up responsibility for the different flower beds. Alex and Benni are very reliable, and Tom is pleased with the quality of their work. Still, he wants to further improve how well his plants grow. After reading in a magazine that fertilizing plants can enhance their growth, he decides to have Alex and Benni fertilize his flowers.
The magazine recommends using either fertilizer A X200R or fertilizer B Y33R, noting that both are particularly effective. At the same time, Tom learns that exposing plants to several different chemicals can sometimes harm them. Therefore, he decides that only one kind of fertilizer should be used in his garden. He chooses A X200R. Tom instructs Alex and Benni to purchase the fertilizer A X200R and to use only this product. Alex offers to buy several bottles of A X200R for both himself and Benni.
A few weeks later, Tom takes a walk through his garden. He notices that some of his plants look healthier: they are more beautiful and larger than before. However, he also observes that some other plants have lost their bright colors and have dried out. This makes Tom very sad and thoughtful. He begins to wonder whether the drying of these plants might be related to the fertilization. To clarify the situation, he talks to Alex and Benni.
Alex reports that he complied with Tom’s instructions and bought and used only the fertilizer A X200R. Benni, however, explains that he instead used the fertilizer B Y33R. He still had several bottles of B Y33R at home and wanted to use them up. Tom then realizes that the plants which dried out were exactly those in the flower beds where both A X200R and B Y33R had been applied by the gardeners. Did the fertilization by Alex cause the plant to dry out?
Options:
- Yes
- No
